finding: | `platform/root/writes.ts:84,93-97,164-180` `claimLock`, `lockHolder`, `acquireLock` | Three races. (1) If the holder releases between a failed `claimLock` and `readEntry`, `current` is undefined. (2) `writeFileSync(..., { flag: 'wx' })` creates the file before it writes the token, so another process can read it empty. Both cases throw "Incomplete lifecycle lock ... Remove it", which tells the user to delete a lock that is gone or still in use. (3) Two writers that see the same stale lock can both pass the check on line 179. The second `unlinkSync` then throws ENOENT, or deletes the lock the first writer just took. | Treat an absent or empty lock as "try again". Take over a stale lock by renaming it aside, which is atomic, instead of checking it and then deleting it. |
outcome: Absent locks retry exclusive creation. Empty locks wait within the initialization budget and remain intact if initialization never finishes. An exclusive recovery-directory lease serializes cooperating stale-lock reclaimers; the holder is read again under that lease before deletion, so a live replacement survives. This uses a lease and recheck instead of the proposed unchecked rename.
verification: Inspected acquireLock, waitForLockInitialization and retireStaleLock. Recovery always releases its lease, rejects an occupied lease, and never unlinks an absent, empty or live lock read under that lease. Successful acquisition records its token; disposal only deletes a still-matching token.

Added five public-root regressions through actual filesystem and process boundaries: release between failed exclusive creation and reading; a real child publishing its token from an empty lock; replacement of a dead holder with a live token before recovery; occupied recovery lease followed by successful correction; and abandoned empty initialization followed by explicit correction. They check live/stale token bytes, lease preservation and removal, owned-lock release and unrelated file preservation. Child commands use the remaining test budget and disposable capture.
